title: indigo_test: the opt-in scheduler and sequencer simulator suites cannot load drivers when indigo_server has no dynamic driver list
description:
Found while implementing ticket 5e7ef4f3 (2026-11-20) for the sequencer suite; confirmed for both suites on master 930aa41ce on 2026-11-22.

indigo_test/integration/run_scheduler_simulators.py and run_sequencer_simulators.py start a private indigo_server and load their drivers through Server.DRIVERS. In a partial build the load never completed: scheduler suite "timed out waiting for agents" (0 of 11), sequencer suite "Timed out waiting for Scripting Agent acceptance results" (no results).

Cause: indigo_server offers only the dynamic drivers listed in build/share/indigo/indigo_drivers (add_drivers()/driver_filter() in indigo_server/indigo_server.c), and only the top-level make all writes that file (Makefile.drvs). Without it Server.DRIVERS has no items to load. Token handling and commit 9f1fc208a, suspected at first, are not involved: the scheduler harness uses no ACL or token, and the sequencer suite's token-authenticated load succeeds at HEAD once the list exists.

Fix: both harnesses fail at once with a message naming the missing drivers and pointing to make all. Two latent test defects exposed once the suites ran were fixed too: sexagesimal() in run_scheduler_simulators.py could print 60.0 seconds, which the scheduler rejects in @target (4 cases), and the sequencer case "meridian flip options readback" read MERIDIAN_FLIP before the agent's update arrived when PAUSE_AFTER_TRANSIT was already set.

outcome.summary: Pass. Root cause verified: indigo_server offers dynamic drivers only from <bin>/../share/indigo/indigo_drivers (indigo_server.c add_drivers/driver_filter, main ~1967-1981), written only under 'make all' (Makefile.drvs:56-58); the ticket worktree build has no build/share/indigo, the primary full build lists all 12 harness drivers; the scheduler harness starts the server without -a, so token handling (9f1fc208a) cannot explain its failure. Early check is correct: Server.DRIVERS items are static + dynamic driver names (indigo_server.c:1083-1092), defined in one defSwitchVector before the wait predicate succeeds, so no false failure on a full build. sexagesimal(): checked 200000 random values in -90..90 plus edge cases (negative, -1e-05, 23.999999 -> 24:00:00.0, -12.999999, carries) - never 60 s/60 min, error <= 0.05 s; 24:00:00.0 is accepted by the scheduler parser (agent_scheduler_header.c:147, max 24 inclusive). Meridian flip: verified the race - set_meridian_flip publishes MERIDIAN_FLIP then set_switch takes the warning path (Sequencer.js:1287-1293, warning() advances with a 0 s timer) when PAUSE_AFTER_TRANSIT is unchanged, so the checkpoint can read the stale indigo_devices copy. Sequence offers no condition-wait step, so a deterministic wait would need new polling machinery in the harness; the fixed 1 s wait follows the 19 existing s.wait() uses in this file and is ample for a local bus round trip - acceptable, non-blocking. Scope limited to 3 test files, no README, whitespace clean, both Python files compile. Did not rerun the simulator suites.

history.previous_description: Found while implementing ticket 5e7ef4f3 (2026-11-20). indigo_test/integration/run_sequencer_simulators.py starts a private indigo_server, but the server refuses the suite's token-authenticated change of Server.DRIVERS, so no driver loads and the run stops before Sequencer.js is sent (0 cases run). The failure is independent of Sequencer.js. Suspected cause: commit 9f1fc208a changed token forwarding after the harness was last updated (not investigated). Consequence: the sequencer_simulators.js cases, including the MERIDIAN_FLIP checks added by 5e7ef4f3 (meridian flip options readback, native-solver flip with enable_meridian_flip(0.15, -0.03) checking AGENT_PLATESOLVER_EXPOSURE 0.15), have never run. Expected: reproduce, fix the harness or the token handling so the suite loads its drivers, then run the full suite and fix any failing case.
history.description:
Found while implementing ticket 5e7ef4f3 (2026-11-20) for the sequencer suite; confirmed for both suites on master 930aa41ce on 2026-11-22.

indigo_test/integration/run_sequencer_simulators.py and indigo_test/integration/run_scheduler_simulators.py start a private indigo_server with an access list (-a) and a token. The server and the drivers load when started by hand and the deliberate unauthenticated probe is refused as intended ("Device 'Server' is protected or locked"), but the suites' token-authenticated loading of drivers through Server.DRIVERS never completes:
- scheduler suite: "timed out waiting for agents", 0 of 11 cases passed;
- sequencer suite: "Timed out waiting for Scripting Agent acceptance results", no results; Sequencer.js is never sent.
Both failures are independent of the Scheduler Agent and Sequencer.js code; the native suites pass (370/370).

Last successful runs: scheduler suite 2026-11-14 (82/82), sequencer suite 2026-09-24 (60/60). Suspected cause, not confirmed: commit 9f1fc208a (2026-11-15, "Locally stamped device or master token may be forwarded to connected remote servers"), which changed token handling in indigo_libs/indigo_bus.c after the harnesses were last updated. Bisect between 2026-11-14 and 9f1fc208a to confirm.

Consequence: the sequencer_simulators.js cases, including the MERIDIAN_FLIP checks added by 5e7ef4f3 (meridian flip options readback, native-solver flip with enable_meridian_flip(0.15, -0.03) checking AGENT_PLATESOLVER_EXPOSURE 0.15), have never run, and the scheduler simulator cases (including the unsafe hold added by a4c962a2/edf38e12) do not run.

Expected: reproduce, establish whether the harness or the bus token handling is wrong (if the bus, keep the security intent of 9f1fc208a and its test_protocol_security.c cases), fix it so both suites load their drivers, then run both full suites and fix any failing case.

history.text: Correction to the description: run_scheduler_simulators.py has no unsafe-hold cases; the unsafe hold is covered only by the native test_agent_scheduler suite. The simulator suite's own 11 cases simply do not run.
Reproducing the scheduler simulator suite failure
Running run_sequencer_simulators.py in the worktree build
Cause: worktree build lacks build/share/indigo/indigo_drivers; scheduler @target 60.0 s bug fixed
Rerunning sequencer case: meridian flip options readback
Running both full simulator suites (scheduler, sequencer) after the fixes

Reproduction and result (implementer). Before: in the ticket worktree build (libs + agents + simulators + indigo_server, no top-level make all) the scheduler suite failed 0/11 'timed out waiting for agents'; the server trace shows defSwitchVector Server.DRIVERS with an empty item list, because indigo_server only offers dynamic drivers listed in build/share/indigo/indigo_drivers (indigo_server/indigo_server.c add_drivers(), main around line 1967-1981), which only the top-level make all writes (Makefile.drvs line 57). The token is not involved: the scheduler suite uses no ACL at all, and the sequencer suite's token-authenticated Server.DRIVERS load succeeded at HEAD (with 9f1fc208a) once the list existed; unauthenticated probes were still refused (Server, Scripting Agent, Configuration Agent). Against the primary checkout's full build the same unchanged scheduler harness loaded all agents. 9f1fc208a is not the cause; no bus change. Fixes: (1) both harnesses now fail at once with a message naming the drivers Server.DRIVERS does not offer and pointing to make all; (2) run_scheduler_simulators.py sexagesimal() printed '+48:16:60.0' (seconds rounded to 60.0), rejected by the scheduler @target parser, failing cases 2-5; it now rounds to the printed tenth first; (3) sequencer_simulators.js 'meridian flip options readback' read MERIDIAN_FLIP before the agent's own update returned through the bus (set_switch skips an unchanged PAUSE_AFTER_TRANSIT without waiting), each checkpoint now waits 1 s. After: scheduler suite 11/11 passed; sequencer suite 136/136 cases passed, 6/6 artifacts, done, no error (no --index-dir, so the solver-dependent selection ran with solver=false); test_protocol_security 24/24 passed in flow check unit; whitespace passed.
